- UP/DOWN: move blocks vertically
- LEFT/RIGHT: move blocks horizontally
The blocks are now at cols 34-38, which is the same column range as the top container. The top container is at rows 9-15, cols 33-39.
Now I need to figure out the goal. Maybe the goal is to move the blocks to match the blue token pattern in the top container? Or maybe the goal is to position the blocks at a specific location.
Let me try moving the blocks up to the top container position and see what happens. The blocks are currently at rows 45-49, cols 34-38. The top container is at rows 9-15, cols 33-39. If I move the blocks up, they should reach the top container.
Actually, looking at the image, the blocks are now at the right side of the gray structure's neck. The neck is at cols 34-35 (narrower part). The blocks are 5 columns wide (cols 34-38), so they extend beyond the neck.
Let me try moving the blocks up to see if they fit into the top container.

# Move blocks up to the top container
# Current position: rows 45-49, cols 34-38
# Top container: rows 9-15, cols 33-39
# Need to move up ~35 rows, which is 7 UP actions (5 rows each)
result = action(['UP', 'UP', 'UP', 'UP', 'UP', 'UP', 'UP'])
ascii = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')

O_positions = [(r, c) for r, line in enumerate(ascii) for c, ch in enumerate(line) if ch == 'O']
b_positions = [(r, c) for r, line in enumerate(ascii) for c, ch in enumerate(line) if ch == 'b' and r > 40]

print(f"After 7 UPs: O rows = {set(r for r, _ in O_positions)}, O cols = {set(c for _, c in O_positions)}")
print(f"After 7 UPs: b rows = {set(r for r, _ in b_positions)}, b cols = {set(c for _, c in b_positions)}")

if result.get('level_completed') or result.get('done'):
    print("Level completed!")

</function>
